comment:
Written from the maker's published source at https://github.com/Vitaocy/VitaocyThings, commit 6f49f84, which the installed plugin.json matches byte for byte. The installed manifest gives no sourceUrl and no manualUrl.

The three amount knobs are plain attenuators over 0 to 1, not attenuverters, so a negative voltage at an input always lowers the control it feeds. The 0.1 depth constant at line 49 means 10V at full amount covers the whole knob range; the README's phrasing, "a ±10 V signal sweeps the entire range", describes a swing of twice that.

The curve exponent runs from 10 at the left of the knob to 0.1 at the right (line 106), and the display's own label calls an exponent above 1.1 LOG and one below 0.9 EXP (line 181). The maker's source comment at line 105 gives the same mapping the other way round, calling 0.1 exponential and 10 logarithmic, which agrees with the display.

All three main knobs and the display read their control input per channel except the display, which uses channel 0 (getCurve at line 80 calls getVoltage rather than getPolyVoltage).

The knob arcs and the curve preview are drawn in drawLayer on custom widgets, so they are readouts rather than controls.

Figures in the lines are literals in src/VOGLI.cpp: the 0.01 and 5 second bounds at lines 46 and 47, the 0.01V detection threshold at line 45, the 0.1 CV depth at line 49.
